output.name: Skarnu
output.myth: When Tavo the Gale came down the north cliffs in the thaw, he snatched the washing off every line. Among it was one red mitten that belonged to Mesk, who was mending the Spindle's nets beside her grandmother. It went up past the Reel, and Aun laughed, then felt bad about laughing, which was the usual order for Aun. He cut the string after it to bring it back, and that is why the string is short. The Turning Gulls, twelve degrees south, saw the whole thing, wheeled, and said nothing, as gulls do. Hesk counted the stitches. Ennu sewed a new one from the sky's cloth, lined with the Down-Mother's down, but it was the wrong colour and would not keep a hand warm. So the Spindle hangs the single mitten on a nail by the hearth, where the Widow's Split-Tail, away to the north-west, can see it. Someone is always looking for the other one. Kael casts his net for it each night and never catches it. Mesk, grown now, says that suits her fine. She only wanted to be asked.
output.finding: From the Widow's Split-Tail, look one hand-span (about 20°) to the south-east for the lone star that hangs by the Spindle's hearth.
